rooms.6718: Shagrat's Shop is a low, smoke-dark room with a ceiling of tarred beams so close overhead that tall customers stoop beneath them. Iron hooks and chains hang from the rafters, and a scarred counter of black oak runs the width of the room, notched by years of blades tested against its edge. A brazier glows in the corner and keeps the place warm and close. The door opens south onto the noise of Bazaar Street.
rooms.6719: Merchant Avenue begins here, where the clamour of Bazaar Street to the west gives way to a broader, better-kept way paved in dressed grey stone. Shopfronts face each other across the street, Atreides's Shop with its bow window to the north and Devilhand's Shop behind a red-painted door to the south. Hanging signs creak on their irons overhead, and the avenue runs on east between rows of merchants' houses. The Temple dome rises pale above the rooftops.
rooms.6720: Atreides's Shop is bright and orderly, lit by a broad bow window whose small panes of bottle glass throw green-tinted light over the floorboards. Tall cabinets with glazed doors line the walls, each shelf labelled in a neat, upright hand, and a brass scale stands polished on the counter. The air smells faintly of beeswax and cedar. The door at the south side lets out onto Merchant Avenue.
rooms.6722: The avenue widens a little here around an old stone horse trough, its water skimmed with fallen leaves and its rim worn smooth by idle hands. Vyrath's Shop stands to the north behind a door studded with iron, while Revenant's Shop to the south keeps its shutters painted a funereal black. Merchant Avenue carries on east and west, its cobbles swept clean each morning by the shopkeepers. Chimney smoke drifts low over the tiled roofs.
rooms.6723: Vyrath's Shop is a narrow, deep room that smells of old parchment, candle wax and something sharper beneath, like struck flint. Shelves climb the walls to the ceiling, reached by a rolling ladder on an iron rail, and a heavy curtain of dark velvet hides a back room from view. A single lamp of green glass burns on the counter. The iron-studded door opens south onto Merchant Avenue.
rooms.6725: Here the avenue grows quieter, for the shops on both sides stand empty, their windows dusty and their doors hung with weathered placards offering them for sale. One empty shopfront waits to the north and another to the south, both with fresh paint on the lintels as if someone hoped to tempt a buyer. Merchant Avenue runs on east and back west toward the busier stretch. A lamp post of black iron stands at the kerb, its glass smoked from years of burning.
rooms.6726: This empty shop has been swept clean and left bare, its floorboards pale where a counter once stood and its walls marked with the ghosts of vanished shelves. Dust motes turn in the light from a single grimy window. A placard nailed inside the door announces that the premises may be had for a fair price from the city's clerks. The door opens south onto Merchant Avenue.
rooms.6728: A row of empty shops lines this stretch of Merchant Avenue, and the street feels hushed after the bustle nearer the bazaar. Weeds have found the cracks between the cobbles, and a broken sign bracket juts from the wall with nothing hanging from it. Vacant shopfronts wait to the north and to the south, each with a faded notice of sale in its window. The avenue goes on east and west.
rooms.6729: The last owner of this shop left in a hurry, by the look of it, for a counter lies on its side against the far wall and a torn ledger cover is nailed to the doorframe as if in spite. The plaster is cracked and stained with damp in one corner, and the room smells of mice and old soot from a cold hearth. Light comes only through the open door, which leads south to Merchant Avenue.
rooms.6731: Merchant Avenue bends here, turning south at a corner where a stone mounting block stands for riders. Tolliver's Shop fills the end of the street to the east, its doorway framed by carved wooden pillars, while an empty shop with boarded windows sits to the north. The avenue runs back west toward the bazaar and on south past more shopfronts. Rainwater from the gutters of the corner house has worn a dark channel down its wall.
rooms.6732: Boards cover the window of this empty shop from the inside, and only thin blades of daylight slip between them to stripe the dusty floor. Someone has chalked a price on the wall and someone else has crossed it out and chalked a lower one. A broken shutter leans in the corner beside a cold, empty fireplace. The way out is south, back onto Merchant Avenue.
rooms.6733: Tolliver's Shop is a warm, crowded room under a high timber roof, its walls hung with racks and pegs and its corners stacked with crates stencilled with the marks of distant ports. A long counter of honey-coloured pine divides the room, scarred with knife cuts and ring stains from countless mugs. Lamps on chains light the place day and night. The carved doorway leads west back onto Merchant Avenue.
rooms.6734: The avenue runs straight here between tall, narrow houses whose upper storeys lean out over the street until their eaves almost touch. Empty shops face each other across the cobbles, one to the east and one to the west, their doors locked and their sills thick with dust. Merchant Avenue continues north to the corner and south toward Luko's Shop at its end. Washing lines strung between the upper windows sway in the breeze.
rooms.6736: A smell of old spice still clings to this empty shop, as though a dealer in peppers and cloves once traded here and the walls kept the memory. Shallow drawers are built into one wall, all of them pulled out and empty, and the floor is stained with rings where barrels stood. Cobwebs thicken in the corners of the low ceiling. The door leads west to Merchant Avenue.
rooms.6737: Merchant Avenue comes to its end here before the painted front of Luko's Shop to the south, where a hanging lantern burns in a cage of brass. An empty shop with a sagging awning stands to the west, and a blank wall of old brick closes off the rest of the street. The avenue leads back north between its rows of shopfronts. Moss grows thick in the shade at the foot of the wall.
rooms.6739: Luko's Shop is cosy and cluttered, a single room with a beamed ceiling and a hearth of round river stones where a fire crackles in all seasons. Shelves run every which way, some slanting, some crooked, all of them packed close, and a painted sign above the counter promises fair dealing. A threadbare rug softens the floor before the hearth. The door opens north onto Merchant Avenue, beneath a brass lantern.
rooms.6738: Rain has found its way into this empty shop through the sagging awning outside, and a dark stain spreads across the floorboards from the threshold. The walls are whitewashed but flaking, and a row of iron hooks along one side hangs empty. An old counter, too heavy to carry off, still squats in the middle of the room under a skin of dust. The door leads east onto Merchant Avenue.
rooms.6735: This little shop is empty but in good repair, with fresh lime on the walls and a new latch on the door, as if the city has made it ready for whoever buys it next. Pale squares on the plaster show where pictures or signs once hung. A small hearth sits cold and swept beneath a plain stone mantel. The way out lies east, onto Merchant Avenue.
rooms.6730: A faint smell of tanned leather lingers in this empty shop, and a workbench scored with awl marks stands abandoned beneath the window. The shelves have been stripped and the hearth is dead, its iron fire-dogs left behind to rust. Light falls grey through panes that no one has washed in a season or two. A warped door swings north onto Merchant Avenue.
rooms.6727: Bare and echoing, this empty shop is larger than it looks from the street, running back into a deep alcove beneath a low arch. The whole place is swept but unfurnished, and every footstep rings off the plaster walls. A bill of sale, curling and yellow, is pasted beside the doorframe. The door leads north to Merchant Avenue.
rooms.6724: Revenant's Shop is dim and hushed behind its black shutters, lit only by tall candles in iron sconces whose flames barely stir. The walls are panelled in dark wood carved with twining thorns, and a glass-topped case runs along the counter, its lock heavy and old. A faint chill hangs in the air that no fire seems to touch. The door leads north back out to Merchant Avenue.
rooms.6721: Devilhand's Shop is a cramped room behind a red-painted door, its walls hung with crimson cloth and its ceiling blackened by the smoke of an oil lamp shaped like a grinning face. A counter of dark stone divides it, worn hollow in the middle by years of coins slid across. Odd charms dangle on cords from the beams and turn slowly in the draught. The red door opens north onto Merchant Avenue.
rooms.6717: Rhinocreed's Shop is built heavy and square, its walls of rough grey stone and its floor of flags laid thick enough to bear an ox. Racks of stout timber stand along the walls, and a great iron-bound chest is bolted to the floor behind the counter. A horned skull of some huge beast is mounted above the hearth, yellow with age. The door leads east out to Bazaar Street.
rooms.6714: Palaon's Shop is airy and light, with a high ceiling hung with a ring of frosted lamps that shine down on a floor of blue and white tiles. Slender shelves of pale ash hold their wares at eye height, and a small fountain trickles into a basin by the counter. The room smells of oranges and clean water. The door opens west onto Bazaar Street.
rooms.6715: Nothing in Erraticus's Shop stands quite straight, for the shelves tilt, the counter leans, and the clocks on the far wall all tell a different hour. Odd contraptions of brass wire and glass hang from the beams, ticking and whirring to themselves. Scorch marks blacken one corner of the ceiling above a cluttered workbench. The crooked door opens east onto Bazaar Street.
rooms.206711: Cardini's Shop is a neat little parlour with a card table of green baize at its centre and velvet drapes drawn across a painted backdrop of stars. Mirrors in gilt frames hang on every wall, so that the lamplight multiplies and the room seems far larger than it is. A tall cabinet with many small drawers stands behind the counter. A curtained doorway leads west onto Bazaar Street.
rooms.206712: Bedlamzer's Shop is a riot of colour and noise, its walls painted in clashing stripes and its rafters hung with bells, ribbons and paper lanterns that jangle whenever the door swings. Wares are heaped on tables in no order anyone but the owner could fathom. A cracked slate by the counter is scrawled with prices in three colours of chalk. The door leads east to Bazaar Street.
rooms.206709: Silvina's Shop is quiet and graceful, its walls washed in pale silver-grey and its floor laid with polished boards that gleam under hanging lamps of pierced silver. Glass cases on slender legs stand in a neat row, and a carved bowl of dried lavender is set into the counter beside a little silver bell. The whole room smells sweetly of it. Its glass-paned door opens west onto Bazaar Street.
rooms.206708: Akaniz's Shop is a long, low room hung with woven rugs from far lands, their reds and ochres faded by sun and smoke. Brass lamps with coloured panes cast patterns across cushions heaped along the walls, and a small charcoal brazier keeps a copper kettle simmering. The smell of strong tea and spice fills the air. The door leads north out onto Bazaar Street.
rooms.206706: Sargoth's Shop is a stark, bare-walled room of dark stone with an iron grille across the counter, behind which the shelves stand in shadow. A forge-black lamp hangs on a chain and swings slightly whenever the door opens. Deep gouges mar the wooden floor, as though something heavy was once dragged across it and out. The door opens north onto Bazaar Street.
rooms.206703: Ruby's Shop glows warm and red, its walls hung with rose-coloured silk and its lamps shaded with garnet glass that turns the light the colour of wine. A cushioned bench runs beneath the window, and a long counter of cherrywood is inlaid with a pattern of small red stones. The faint scent of roses lingers about the place. The door leads north onto Bazaar Street.
rooms.203112: Park Road runs straight here between low garden walls overhung with ivy and the branches of old fruit trees grown up behind them. The cobbles are uneven where roots have heaved them, and a stone drinking fountain set in the wall dribbles into a mossy basin. The road goes on north toward a bend and south toward the crossing with Elm Street. The scent of cut grass drifts over the walls.
rooms.3142: High in the branches of a great elm, a broad fork makes a natural seat where generations of city children have carved their initials into the grey bark. Leaves rustle on every side and sunlight flickers through them, and through gaps in the green you can see the rooftops and the city wall beyond. The trunk is knobbed with old footholds that lead down to the end of Elm Street below. The branches sway gently with the wind.
rooms.203075: The Gate Of The Inner City opens here through the thickness of the wall, a deep arch of grey stone with a portcullis hanging raised above, its iron teeth rusted brown. Two round towers flank the passage and banners of Garathorm stir high on their parapets. A narrow stair climbs up inside the tower to the walk along the city wall. The Concourse lies north within the walls, and the Trade Road runs out south into open country.
rooms.3143: Here the Concourse passes beneath a long vaulted arcade built against the city wall, its roof held on stout stone piers and its floor paved with worn flags. Lamps in iron cages hang from the vault, burning even at midday, and the noise of the street echoes along the arches. Stalls once stood between the piers, and their sockets still pock the floor. The arcade opens east onto the Concourse near Emerald Avenue and west toward the corner where the wall turns.
rooms.203151: The Concourse turns north here from the corner of the city wall and runs along its inner face, the great stones rising sheer and grey on one side of the street. Lean-to sheds and cobblers' stalls huddle against the foot of the wall, their roofs patched with sacking. The way goes on north along the wall and back south to the corner. Smoke from the stalls' braziers hangs in the still air.
rooms.203150: A watering trough cut from a single block of granite stands against the wall here, fed by a lead pipe that drips steadily from a lion's-head spout. The cobbles around it are always wet and dark, and moss grows green in their joints. The Concourse runs north and south along the inner face of the wall, between it and a row of tall, shuttered houses. Somewhere nearby a smith's hammer rings.
rooms.3149: This stretch of the Concourse is lined with rope-makers' and chandlers' yards, their gates open on the street and the smell of tar and hemp heavy on the air. The city wall looms over them, streaked dark where rainwater runs down from the battlements. A worn stone marker set into the wall shows the height of some long-ago flood. The Concourse goes on north and back south.
rooms.3148: The Concourse narrows here where a guardhouse of squat stone juts from the wall, its single window barred and its door painted with the arms of Garathorm. A bench beside the door is polished by the seats of off-duty watchmen. Pigeon-grey slates cover the roofs of the houses across the way. The street leads north toward the turning for Park Road and south along the wall.
rooms.3147: Park Road branches off east here from the Concourse, passing beneath a stone archway carved with leaves and fruit, and through it you can glimpse the green of garden trees. The Concourse itself goes on north and south along the wall, busier at this corner where carts turn in and out. Iron bollards protect the corners of the arch, scarred by many a careless wheel. A notice board on the archway is plastered with handbills.
rooms.3146: Washerwomen's troughs line the foot of the wall along this part of the Concourse, a long stone channel fed by a culvert where soapy water foams and gurgles away into a drain. Lines of washing are strung across the street between iron pegs driven into the wall. The air is damp and smells of lye. The Concourse runs on north and back south toward Park Road.
rooms.3145: Here the Concourse runs quiet and shaded, the wall on one hand and the blind backs of warehouses on the other, so that little sun reaches the cobbles. A carved boundary stone at the kerb marks where one ward of the city ends and another begins. Dandelions push up between the paving stones. The street goes on north toward the bridge end and south along the wall.
rooms.3144: The Concourse draws near the end of its run along the wall here, and the sound of the river can be heard ahead past the rooftops. A tall stone column stands at the roadside topped with a weathered bronze lantern, lit each evening by the lamplighters. Cart ruts are worn deep into the cobbles. The street continues north to the end of the Concourse by the bridge and south along the wall.
rooms.9784: Academy Path sets out from the city here, a lane of packed earth and scattered cobbles leading away from the towers of the West Gate, which lie just south. North, the lane gives out at the edge of a dark forest whose old oaks stand thick and shadowed, while the path itself bends west toward the School House. A wooden signpost leans at the fork, its arms weathered grey. Wild grass grows tall along the verges.
rooms.9785: The path runs beside a broad hawthorn hedge here, worn into a shallow trough by the feet of scholars coming and going. Through gaps in the hedge you glimpse a close-cropped meadow, and the city wall shows grey beyond the fields. The way turns north toward the School House and back east to the signpost by the forest's edge. Wildflowers dot the banks.
rooms.9786: Academy Path climbs a gentle rise here, its ruts filled with gravel to spare the boots of students in the wet. An old milestone at the verge has been carved over with initials and doodles, its proper inscription long since worn away. Ahead to the north the roof and bell-cote of the School House show above the trees, and the path drops back south toward the hedges. A breeze stirs the long grass.
rooms.9787: The path ends here in a small swept yard before the Garathorm School House, a long building of honey-coloured stone with tall windows and a bell-cote perched on its roof. Its heavy double doors stand open to the north beneath a carved lintel. A slate board by the gate lists the day's lessons in a schoolmaster's careful hand, and Academy Path runs back south through the grass. Scuffed hopscotch squares are scratched into the flags of the yard.
rooms.203076: The Undertaker's Workshop is a long, cool room smelling of sawdust, pitch and dried herbs. Coffins in every stage of making lean against the walls, from bare planks to finished caskets lined with black cloth, and a heavy workbench stands under a window of thick, greenish glass. A lamp burns low before a small shrine set in an alcove of the far wall. The door opens west onto Wall Road, in the shadow of the city wall.
rooms.203048: The Silver Goblet Tavern is a low-beamed taproom, dim and close, with a sagging ceiling stained brown by pipe smoke and a fire smouldering in a wide hearth. Battered tables and benches crowd the sawdust floor, and a dented silver goblet, the tavern's namesake, hangs on a chain above the bar. Quiet corners with high-backed settles suit those who would rather not be seen. The door leads east out into The Dark Alley.
rooms.3000: The Temple Library is a long marble hall lined from floor to vaulted ceiling with oaken bookcases, their shelves crowded with tomes, scrolls and bound records of the realm. Reading desks stand in rows beneath hanging lamps, and a deep hush lies over everything. Archways lead north to the Map Room and south to the Hall of Champions, the temple hall opens east, and a door on the west gives onto The Gate Of Fameland. The smell of old vellum and lamp oil fills the air.
rooms.3070: Maps cover every wall of this square chamber, painted and pinned and pasted one over another until the plaster vanishes beneath coastlines, rivers and roads. A great table in the centre bears a relief of Misthollow modelled in painted clay, its mountains and forests raised in miniature. A door north opens on the Cartographer's Study, a low arch west leads into the Keymaster's Workshop, and the library lies south. Brass lamps hang low over the table.
rooms.3079: The Cartographer's Study is a cramped, cluttered room where a slanting drafting desk stands beneath a lamp with a polished reflector. Rolled charts are stacked in pigeonholes along the walls, and the desk's surface is scarred with compass pricks and splashed with ink. An unfinished map of some far coast is pinned to the desk, its edges still blank. The only door leads south to the Map Room.
rooms.203082: The Keymaster's Workshop is a narrow room smelling of oil and iron filings, its walls hung with board after board of hooks where countless keys once hung, many now bare. A small anvil and a vice are fixed to a sturdy bench beneath a lamp, and a rack of fine files stands beside them. Locks of every size, taken apart, are mounted on the wall like trophies. The doorway leads east back to the Map Room.
rooms.203081: The Hall of Champions is a lofty chamber of white marble where the names of the realm's great heroes are carved in gilded letters on tall tablets along the walls. Banners of past deeds hang tattered from the gallery rails, and a ring of empty plinths awaits statues not yet raised. A spiral stair climbs up into the Tower of Champions, and the library lies back north through a high arch. Candles burn steadily in iron stands.
rooms.203083: The Tower of Champions is a round room at the top of a spiral stair, its walls pierced by tall arched windows that look out over the rooftops of Garathorm to the hills beyond. Shields of fallen heroes are hung about the walls, each painted with its bearer's arms. A brazier on a bronze tripod burns in the centre of the floor. The stair winds down to the Hall of Champions.

6717.description: The skull is longer than a man's arm, with a single thick horn curving up from the snout and a second, broken stump behind it. Someone has rubbed the bone with oil until it shines like old ivory.

203075.description: The portcullis is a lattice of oak beams shod in iron, its lower edge ending in a row of rusted spikes. Its chains run up into slots in the arch, and it has not been lowered in living memory.

203150.description: The bronze lion's head is green with age, its mane worn smooth and its jaws gaping. A steady trickle of water falls from its mouth into the trough below.

9786.description: Beneath the scratched initials and crude drawings you can just make out a carved number and the faint shape of an open book, the old sign of the School House.

203048.description: The goblet is tarnished nearly black and dented on one side, as if it once stopped a blow. Its chain is fixed fast to a beam above the bar.

3070.description: The clay relief shows the whole of the known realm, from the walls of Garathorm to the Sea of Storms. Some regions at its edges are left unpainted and blank.

203081.description: The tablets are cut from pale marble, each name picked out in gold leaf. Many tablets stand still smooth and empty, waiting for names yet to be earned.
